Mission: Discover a genuinely new physical mechanism capable of enabling an exceptional, civilisation-changing scientific or technological advance.
Begin independently. Do not default to Astra's previous ionic pumps, catalytic oscillators, hBN defect repair or hypothetical excitation-recycling devices.
Investigate several exceptionally important technological limitations in energy, chemistry, synthesis, materials, manufacturing, electronic devices or other foundational fields.
Use two complementary searches:
Capability-first: Identify a transformation or scientific operation existing technology cannot achieve with acceptable energy, selectivity, precision, cost or damage.
Mechanism-first: Investigate experimentally established but underexploited physical responses that might permit an entirely unfamiliar operation.
Choose an opportunity where new physics could produce an exceptional advantage.
Identify a real material, molecular structure or experimentally accessible physical system.
Derive the required mechanism and its competing processes from a consistent physical description.
Do not independently choose favourable transition rates, coupling strengths, excited-state populations, control fields or lifetimes.
An established optical transition is not evidence of a useful chemical reaction. Enhanced mobility is not evidence of directed or retained modification.
Seek mathematical and physical principles beyond existing device architectures.
Compare the proposed operation against the strongest actual method for the same desired outcome.
Determine whether the advantage concerns a genuinely inaccessible transformation, radically better selectivity, lower damage, energy efficiency, throughput or another meaningful scientific capability.
Do not claim novelty for an established effect merely because its driving protocol is different.
Identify the smallest experimentally accessible observation capable of distinguishing the proposed mechanism from the strongest competing explanation.
Make quantitative predictions using acquired or independently supportable parameters.
Investigate coupled material feasibility, fabrication, environmental stability, damage, energy consumption and scaling.
If the selected mechanism lacks physical leverage, replace it instead of extending optimistic simulations.

## Disposition and exact source contract

Preserve this work as a specific, falsifiable physical hypothesis and a checked
kinematic audit. Its proposed output is a retained basis-resolved occupancy or
conversion imbalance under a broad, phase-locked electron beam. It establishes
neither an acquired elemental-Te retained-event law nor useful addressing,
throughput, room-temperature retention, manufacturing advantage or historical
priority. It does not establish a civilization-enabling breakthrough.

The initial paste contains 165 lines. The subsequently supplied
`astra_phonon_recoil_audit.zip` contains README, arithmetic code and reported JSON;
it supplies no Hamiltonian, trajectory ensemble or defect-yield data. All three
files were read. The script was copied to private scratch before replay.
The 43 numeric leaves and 12 other leaves agree within stated tolerance;
one hazard-ratio value differs by 1.24e-16 relative roundoff. The preserved
producer JSON is not byte-identical to replay output. See `REPLAY_RECEIPT.json`.
No producer hash manifest was supplied. Intake hashes are provenance, not a
producer signature or independent scientific validation.

This is a new mechanism hypothesis alongside N774, rather than a demonstration
of its ionic pump. N774's phase-odd direct-force counterexample remains a warning
against identifying a mechanism from phase contrast alone. N777 supplies the
configuration-level committor/control distinction; N783 supplies full-state,
terminal retained-reward accounting. None supplies the missing Te reaction law.
The three new conditional constructions below are integration-derived. They
apply standard optimization, Gaussian testing and controlled competing-risk
reasoning; they are not priority claims for those mathematical subjects.
